summary:
One of the most significant issues in the city of La Paz is landslides.
In response to this threat, our team, DX Force, proposes a digital platform designed to inform the public about landslide risks. The platform also includes an early warning system, which operates based on NASA satellite data—utilizing SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) tools, digital elevation models, and historical data records.
details: This is an interactive web platform designed to inform end-users and help them take precautions against potential landslides. A key benefit is that it enables individuals to avoid landslide-prone areas, thereby protecting lives during mass movement events, preventing further negative consequences, and improving quality of life through effective risk management. For this project, we utilized Geographic Information Systems (QGIS), Google Earth Engine, VS Code, Copilot, Claude, NASA raster data, and NASA digital elevation models, employing the following programming languages: JavaScript, Python, HTML, CSS, and SQL. The project features 3D modeling and simulation of locations where major landslides have occurred, an alert system that allows users to report landslides or similar events (within a controlled safety margin), and an immediate notification feature for when a landslide takes place. The factors considered include terrain slope, ground displacement data obtained via SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar), historical landslide records (2000–2026), and proximity to the nearest rivers and the link of the web page is "https://ladera-la-paz.proyectonasa.workers.dev/#explorer''
